topic: The Geometric Bridge: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Visualization (1 min)
lecture_lines: Consider a sphere in bright, direct sunlight.
Its shadow on the ground is a circle.
The shadow's radius matches the sphere's radius.
animations: Create a circle with color #FF00FF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: Connecting Area to Projection (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Archimedes proved the sphere equals a circumscribed cylinder.
This cylinder's surface area is four circles.
The sphere's surface is four times its shadow.
Mathematically, this equals four pi r squared.
Geometry links the surface to the shadow.
animations: Show a flat rectangle in #00FFFF, represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Project the rectangle onto a line segment.
Label the projection 'Shadow' in white, transitioning towards [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cylinder.svg].

sections.title: The Calculus Logic (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Think of the sphere as thin horizontal rings.
Project these rings onto the circumscribing cylinder.
The cylinder's area equals the sphere's area.
Everything sums up to four shadow areas.
animations: Draw tiny vertical rectangles, represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cylinder.svg], under the curve.
Sum up the areas of these rectangles.

sections.title: Real-World Application (1 min)
lecture_lines: Sphere surface area is four times the shadow.
Measure a planet's disk to find its area.
This rule applies to any sphere.
animations: Animate a bridge structure using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] in #00FF00.
Highlight the stress load on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg].
Label the load 'Tension' in white over the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg].
